**What this is.** A record of past work, not a plan. From 2026-09-11 to 2026-09-22 PHGv2 (2.5.14) was used to
impute the BC2S3 skim lines of donor Zd.0040_P1 (and Zx.0100_P4) on chromosome 10. The PHG calls were then
compared with RTIGER and with two nilHMM callers. This notebook covers, in date order, the founder sets
that were tried, the PHG problems met along the way, the `find-paths` settings and why they changed, the
2026-09-22 stay × F grid, the structural no-call, and the four-caller comparison on the introgressed Zd.0040
lines. Every number comes from the files named in each section's "Sources" line. Where the sources disagree,
the later decision wins, and the superseded one is named.

::: {.callout-note}
## Outcome (what holds on 2026-09-22)

- **Graph:** per donor, **two founders**, B73 + the donor's synthetic haplotype H_d. The taxon founder was
  dropped on 09-18. The reference ranges are **lowcopy** (gene ±500 bp ∪ non-TE intergenic; 8,095 ranges on
  chr10). The gene-only ranges of 09-18 were superseded on 09-20/21.
- **PHG founder:** Zd.0040_P1 v4, the A+B founder witnessed by the BC2S3 pool, **103,809 alleles**
  (decision of 09-21 01:50).
- **find-paths:** **F = 0, stay (`--prob-same-gamete`) 0.99999**, min-reads 1. This is the setting for pools,
  because the BC2S3 skims are 6-plant field-plot bulks. The user fixed it after the 09-22 stay × F grid (job
  921951). The grid barely varied (DSC 0.718–0.744) and was best at stay 0.99 / F 0.2 (DSC 0.744, MCC 0.697).
- **No-call is structural:** 22% in every grid cell. In 1,657 of 8,095 ranges the B73 and donor haplotypes
  are identical, and in 33 more the donor has no haplotype. This comes from the founder. find-paths settings
  cannot change it.
- **Comparison:** RTIGER, PHG (F = 0), nnil and bbnil were painted on the six RTIGER-introgressed Zd.0040 lines
  plus the B73 control. PHG no-call ranges are bridged (RLE and fill) for display. All callers are also
  back-projected onto the 103,809 informative founder markers. Among the count callers, bbnil is closest to
  RTIGER and nnil is speckled. The B73 control is clean in all four callers.
- **Known PHG defects:** dosage under-call (ALT → HET) and fragmentation. zealhmm `R/metrics.R`
  (`rasterize_states`, `marker_dsc`) is the canonical scorer. Marker-level scoring is parked; for now only the
  painting was needed.
:::

# 1. PHG setup: founder sets tried

The first design used **per-taxon founders**: B73 NAM v5 plus five PanAnd teosinte assemblies, one per taxon
(Zx-TIL18, Zv-TIL11, Zd-Gigi, Zl-RIL003, Zh-RIMHU001). The chr10 pilot was meant to measure the resources of a
full build. Of the five, only **Gigi and TIL18** were aligned to B73 and loaded into the chr10 DB
(`vcf_dbs`: B73, Gigi, TIL18). The per-taxon founder design was marked "NOT decided" from the start.

On 09-17/18 PHGv2 turned out to store a haplotype only as sequence in the AGC archive, and `gvcf2hvcf` pulls
that sequence through ASM_* coordinates. So the donor founder was built as a **pseudo-assembly on B73
coordinates**: B73 chr10 with the donor's tier A/B alleles written in by `bcftools consensus`. It was loaded
into a copy of the pilot DB, and the imputation graph had three founders (B73 + taxon + donor).

| date | founder set / graph | ranges | donor alleles (chr10) | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 09-11/12 | per-taxon: B73 + Gigi + TIL18 (2 of 5 staged) | gene ± 500 | — | DB build only |
| 09-17/18 | 3 founders: B73 + taxon + H_d pseudo-assembly | 4,685 (H_d has haplotypes in 2,517 Zd / 2,516 Zx) | Zd 128,302; Zx 106,868 (tiers A+B) | works end to end; dosage under-call and fragmentation |
| 09-18 | **2 founders: B73 + H_d**, taxon dropped | 2,489 gene ranges (donor 2,473) | 128,302 | agreement with RTIGER fell (see §4) |
| 09-19 | 2 founders, strict founder v2 (alt in > 1 pool) | gene-only | 75,014 | introgressed 84.8 → 87.4% agree |
| 09-20 | 2 founders, union (lowcopy) ranges | 8,095 (26.0 Mb; haplotypes in 8,062 Zd / 8,058 Zx) | Zd 166,789; Zx 140,365; v3 174,725 | introgressed 87.3%, clean 99.9% |
| 09-21 | founder **v4**: BC2S3 pool as required witness | 8,095 | **103,809** (A+B) | 89.6% vs poolseq RTIGER |
| 09-21 | founder v5: tier A only | 8,095 | 48,791 | 88.2%; PHG keeps v4 |

The taxon founder was dropped on 09-18. It had stood in for the intergenic ranges where H_d had no
haplotype, and the paths alternated B73/H_d ↔ B73/taxon from range to range. The result was dosage
under-call and fragmentation. It is also another accession, with about 50% allele match. The user ruled out
an all-donor graph and a taxon fallback in the imputation graph. Ranges the donor lacks must show as missing,
never as B73 or taxon. PHG 2.5.14 has no per-sample ancestor input, so the graph is restricted at export
(`export-vcf --sample-names B73,<donor>`).

The ranges changed twice. The **gene-only** set came first, from the 09-18 memory note. The **lowcopy/union**
set was decided on 09-20 and kept on 09-21, when fixed 1 Mb and 250 kb bins were rejected because they gave a
false HET background. So any "gene-only ranges" in the 09-18 notes is superseded.

Sources: agent/PHG_PILOT_chr10.md; agent/pilot_1B_chr10_runlog_20260917.md (09-17 → 09-21 sections);
docs/PROJECT_STATE.md; docs/DECISIONS.md (09-18, 09-20, 09-21); memory per-donor-imputation-graph,
phg-founder-assemblies, pilot-1b-chr10-phg-route.

# 2. PHG facts and pitfalls

These all came up during the chr10 build and imputation.

| issue | what happened | fix |
|---|---|---|
| `agc append` | PHG's `agc-compress` appends when the archive exists. Ranged `agc getctg <contig>@<donor>:a-b` then aborts (core dump) for the appended donor; whole-contig retrieval works | move the old archive aside and **re-create** it with all founders |
| `gvcf2hvcf` query batching | the default `--num-ranges-per-agc-query -1` makes one `agc` call per range. It ran 88 min with no output (TIMEOUT) | `--num-ranges-per-agc-query 500`: 5,808 ranges in 12 queries, gvcf2hvcf in 1 min |
| keyfile header | `map-kmers` requires the camelCase column `sampleName`, though `--help` says `samplename` | camelCase keyfiles |
| shared haplotypes | in 1,657 of 8,062 union ranges the donor haplotype is byte-identical to B73 (same hapid). PHG reports the range under B73's name, and the first parser counted it as B73/B73 | treat shared-hapid ranges as **no call** (`pilot_step9_compare_rtiger_v5.R`) |
| `hvcf2vcf` | needs a pangenome VCF; no `--regions` or `--sample-names` option | see §7.4 |

Two checks confirmed that the founder reaches the graph. At 5 tier-A positions, B73 has the REF base and the
pseudo-assembly has the ALT base. In the one-range test, 2,006 of 2,006 Zd ranges with a tier-A site have a
hapid that differs from B73 (0 identical), and for Zx 2,135 of 2,135. On 09-21 01:05, the shared-hapid
parsing error was found to account for 2,380 of 9,061 (26%) B73 calls inside RTIGER-50K teosinte blocks.
Excluding shared ranges left the 1 Mb agreement unchanged (89.6 introgressed, 100 clean, B73 check 0 bins).
The shared ranges had received almost no reads in any case.

Sources: agent/pilot_1B_chr10_runlog_20260917.md (attempts 3–5, "PHG 2.5.14 facts", 09-21 01:05 and 01:14);
memory pilot-1b-chr10-phg-route; 09-22 session transcript.

# 3. The BC2S3 skims are 6-plant bulks

On 09-19, around 01:20, the user established that each BC2S3 skim is a **6-plant bulk from one field plot**.
The pedigrees are single-plant descents (P#.1.1.1), and the 6 plants per skim are S3 sibs of one S2 plant, so a
skim holds 12 sampled haplotypes. The per-range H_d read fraction agreed:

- Zd00401454's ALT block peaks at 0.9–1.0 (a fixed family).
- Zd00401431's HET block centres on 0.3–0.4 (about 4–5 of 12 haplotypes teosinte).
- Zd00401111 is flat from 0 to 1.

It followed that PHG's diploid `find-paths` (fractions 0 / 0.5 / 1) is mis-specified for a segregating pool.
On 09-19 ~02:00 the user corrected one inference. Bulking does raise HET (any unfixed region). But it does not
by itself create B73 runs under independent Poisson sampling, and the B73 runs seen then were line-specific.

The 09-22 simulation took this further. 6-plant equimolar bulks at k/12 dosage were simulated, and a sweep
from the same founders was imputed (Gigi graphs; plot qc05). PHG **shreds the segregating block** at both
1.2x and 0.05x, while the fixed block (qc04) stays solid in every lane. The earlier single-genome sweep had
stayed clean. The qc05 F sweep then found the cause in the inbreeding prior: F = 0.0–0.2 matches the truth
best, F = 0.3–0.9 adds REF gaps and stripes, and F = 1.0 collapses into REF/ALT slivers with no HET.

The user concluded that at λ = 0.05, **F = 0 is the only setting that keeps the HET fragment whole**. That is
the setting that reconstructs the BC2S2 segregation of the BC2S3 pools, called the "pool setting" from here on.

Sources: agent/pilot_1B_chr10_runlog_20260917.md (09-19 01:20 and the correction at ~02:00); 09-22 session
transcript (6-plant bulk arm, qc05 F sweep job 920401, paintings job 920413); git log 09-22 (read_mixing
bulk sweep, breakpoint_sim_bulk, f_sweep_qc05).

# 4. find-paths settings over time

| when | stay (`--prob-same-gamete`) | F (`--inbreeding-coefficient`) | min-reads | graph / founder | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 09-17/18 first pilot | 0.99 (default) | default | — | 3-founder | location right, dosage under-call, fragmentation |
| 09-18 night (v2) | **0.9999** | **0.86** | 1 | gene-only 2-founder | Zd mean agree 91.9 → 84.9, Zx 93.3 → 91.8; B73 check 0 → 12 teosinte bins |
| 09-18 rerun (v3) | 0.99 | 0.86 | 1 | same | agree within ±1.5 of both earlier runs: calls did not depend on stay |
| 09-19 – 09-20 (v4 strict, union v5/v6) | 0.99 | 0.86 | 1 | strict / union | the "PHG_A" setting |
| 09-20 22:28 | **0.9991** | 0.86 | 1 | union v3 | stay at the genetic value; Zd introgressed 87.2 → 87.5 |
| 09-21 (founders v4, v5) | 0.9991 | 0.86 | 1 | union v4 / v5 | 89.6% (v4) / 88.2% (v5) vs poolseq RTIGER |
| 09-22 (real Zd.0040, job 921443) | 0.9991 | **0** | 1 | union v4 | segregating blocks become continuous HET |
| 09-22 (job 921723) | **0.99999** | **0** | 1 | union v4 | longer HET runs; kept |

The 0.86 value was chosen to match RTIGER's 15% HET among teosinte loci. PHG's F is the start weight on
homozygous pairs plus a per-range HET penalty of about |ln(1−F)|. The 0.9991 value came from the genetic rate:
the zealtiger fit gives λ = 4.72 per Morgan as the exit rate.

On 09-20 a simulation contrasted "PHG B" (stay 0.9999, F = 0) with the user's setting "A" (0.99/0.86/1). With
a single-genome truth, F = 0 needed only 15% non-informative sites to turn ALT into HET. That was before the
skims were modelled as bulks. On 09-22 the 6-plant-bulk result replaced the F = 0.86 setting with F = 0.

The user's reading of the 09-22 real-data F = 0 paintings was that the higher stay together with F = 0 captures
the HET of the segregating pools, at the cost of more B73-background HET and weaker homozygous-ALT calls.
Old (unfiltered) and MAPQ20 reads gave almost identical PHG paintings at every setting tried, so read
filtering does not drive the pattern.

Sources: agent/pilot_1B_chr10_runlog_20260917.md (09-18 night, step7_v3, 09-20 20:50, 21:25, 22:28, 09-21
00:44, 01:44); memory per-donor-imputation-graph; 09-22 session transcript (jobs 921413/921443, 921723);
git log 09-21/22 (phg_lane_mapq20, real_zd0040_F0).

# 5. The 2026-09-22 stay × F grid on Zd.0040_P1

The user asked for the setting that maximizes classification performance, **with the RTIGER track treated as
truth**. The objective was **DSC**, the user's name for macro-F1 (the mean per-class Dice
2TP / (2TP + FP + FN) over REF / HET / ALT), with multiclass MCC as a chance-corrected check. The grid had
5 stay values {0.99, 0.999, 0.9991, 0.9999, 0.99999} and 3 F values {0, 0.1, 0.2}, giving 15 find-paths cells
on the MAPQ20 reads with the read-mappings reused (job 921830). It was scored per reference range over all
lines by `PHG/analysis/score_stayF_grid.R` (job 921943). The first MCC came out NA from integer overflow; it
was recast as a double and rerun as job 921951.

The **B73 control is included** in the score. The user pointed out that it is a real imputation and measures
the baseline error. No-call ranges are left out of the confusion matrix and reported separately.

| rank | stay | F | DSC | Dice REF / HET / ALT | HET recall / precision | ALT recall / precision | no-call |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.99 | 0.2 | **0.744** (MCC **0.697**) | .98 / .60 / .66 | .73 / .51 | .50 / .96 | 0.22 |
| 8 | 0.99 | 0.0 | 0.735 | .98 / .60 / .63 | .76 / .49 | .47 / .98 | 0.22 |
| 15 | 0.99999 | 0.0 | 0.718 | .98 / .62 / .55 | .79 / .49 | .51 / .99 | 0.22 |

What the grid shows: DSC is almost flat (0.72–0.74), so the setting matters little on this metric. HET is the
weak class in every cell (Dice about 0.60, precision about 0.50). F = 0.2 edges out F = 0 through ALT recall.
No-call is 22% in every cell.

The **parameters were fixed at F = 0, stay 0.99999** (the pool setting), which is the rank-15 cell. The grid
does not overturn that choice, because the scores barely move. On 09-23 the user rejected a proposal to tune
min-reads, F or stay again, since that had already been done. What PHG can still change is the founder, not the
`find-paths` parameters.

Sources: headers of PHG/analysis/score_stayF_grid.R; git log 09-22 (4e6092e, 94006a8); 09-22 session
transcript (grid table, jobs 921830/921943/921951); memory phg-stay-f-grid-insensitive.

# 6. The 22% no-call is structural

Of the **8,095** chr10 lowcopy ranges, **1,657 (20.5%)** have identical B73 and donor haplotypes (same hapid),
and **33** more have no donor haplotype. Together that is the 22%, flat across the whole grid.

The user asked how there could be non-informative ranges when every founder allele is informative. The answer
is that ranges and markers are different things. The ranges are B73-annotation intervals, defined before any
variant is called. A range that received no founder allele gets only reference blocks, so its donor haplotype
is byte-identical to B73. There are two reasons a range gets no allele: the donor matches B73 there, or
discovery missed the variation (no CRISP record, vetoed, below tier, no pool reads). Nobody measured how the
1,657 split between the two.

Sources: 09-22 session transcript; memory phg-stay-f-grid-insensitive; agent/pilot_1B_chr10_runlog_20260917.md
(09-21 01:05, 01:14).

# 7. Callers compared on the introgressed Zd.0040 lines

## 7.1 The four lanes

The six lines with more than 10% of chr10 in RTIGER introgression were PN7_SID628, SID590, SID595, SID608,
SID615 and SID592. They were painted together with the B73 control PN10_SID893, which is pinned on top.
Script: `PHG/analysis/paint_callers_introg.R` (job 921906).

| lane | what it is | input / settings |
|---|---|---|
| RTIGER | reference track | RTIGER segments, chr10 |
| PHG (F = 0) | two-founder graph, founder v4 | `_imputed_parents.txt`; shared-hapid ranges set to no call |
| nnil | called-genotype HMM | `call_gt(prior = "flat")` → `call_ancestry(caller = "nnil", design = "BC2S3")` on founder-site counts |
| bbnil | BetaBinomial HMM | `call_ancestry(caller = "bbnil", design = "BC2S3", rrate = 1e-4, err = 0.01)` on the same counts |

LB-Impute was considered and not run: the user asked for nnil and bbnil only.

## 7.2 Bridging the PHG no-call ranges

In the first painting the PHG lane was sparse. Only ranges with a call were drawn, so the no-call ranges read
as fragmentation. The fix came in two commits. `b4662db` RLE-bridged the PHG no-call ranges into continuous
segments. That still left white gaps, because the lowcopy ranges are not contiguous and the no-calls are
scattered. The user objected ("the PHG track is full of missing data"), and `daac32b` filled each no-call range
with the flanking ancestry (`nafill` locf then nocb) and extended the track from 0 to the chromosome length.
The PHG lane is now gap-free.

The white left in the nnil and bbnil lanes is **not missing data**. Those callers are Viterbi HMMs with no
missing state. Their `g` has 0 NA and they see the same observed markers. The white is the space between
marker-narrow segments (job 922405):

| line | observed markers | nnil segments / interior gap | bbnil segments / interior gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zd00401542 | 52,465 | 3,261 / 29.4 Mb | 284 / 3.5 Mb |
| Zd00401111 | 56,606 | 2,514 / 11.6 Mb | 922 / 5.6 Mb |
| Zd00401544/615 (as labelled in the output) | 54,935 | 631 / 4.7 Mb | 411 / 3.9 Mb |

The speckle in nnil comes from forcing a hard diploid genotype onto a pool. Whether to draw nnil as
contiguous was left as an open question to the user.

![RTIGER / PHG (F = 0, bridged) / nnil / bbnil on the six RTIGER-introgressed Zd.0040_P1 lines plus the B73 control, chr10.](../../agent/qcset_designB_results/callers_introg/Zd0040_introg_RTIGER_PHG_nnil_bbnil.png)

Reading of the bridged painting (09-22): PHG shows continuous segments that match RTIGER (Zd00401542 a solid
HET block, Zd00401454 a solid ALT block, Zd00401114 the distal ALT block). bbnil follows RTIGER as continuous
blocks, nnil stays speckled, and the B73 control is clean REF in all four lanes.

## 7.3 Back-projection onto the informative founder markers

The user asked to put all callers on the same positions. `PHG/analysis/paint_markers_introg.R` (commit
`64470f1`, job 922053) does this in four steps:

1. Take the informative marker set, the **103,809** founder v4 alleles.
2. Give each marker the state of the PHG range it falls in, and read RTIGER, nnil and bbnil at the same
   positions.
3. RLE the per-marker states into segments, with boundaries at the midpoints between markers. `paint_calls`
   is interval-based, so single markers would draw as 1-bp slivers.
4. Paint.

![All four callers back-projected onto the 103,809 informative founder markers and RLE'd into segments.](../../agent/qcset_designB_results/callers_introg/Zd0040_introg_markers_RTIGER_PHG_nnil_bbnil.png)

Back-projection does not reduce fragmentation. It changes the sampling grid so that all callers share one
axis, and the ranges without markers drop out. A first measurement found 1,130 markers (1.1%) inside shared
ranges and a mean PHG no-call at markers of 6.3% (3.5–10.0% across the 39 lines), falling with coverage (job
922107). The user objected that a variant site cannot, by construction, sit in an interval with no variant. The
session then attributed most of the 6.3% to the projection's own handling of range edges and the NA rule for
shared ranges, and only the 1,130 markers to a real mismatch between the founder table and the graph. That
split was stated but not measured separately.

## 7.4 The native export detour, and why the back-projection is equivalent

The PHG docs list two exports after `find-paths`:

- **`hvcf2gvcf`** was rejected by the user. A gVCF writes non-variant stretches as reference blocks, so
  informative sites that PHG imputes as B73 would disappear into those blocks.
- **`hvcf2vcf`** emits a genotype at every pangenome position, but it needs `--pangenome-vcf-file` built by
  `merge-gvcfs`. It has no region or sample flag: samples are restricted through the `--hvcf-dir` contents and
  positions through the pangenome VCF. A run scoped to the 6 lines plus the B73 control (job 922158) failed
  because **`merge-gvcfs` writes one VCF per reference range**
  (`pangenome.vcf-chr10_<start>-<end>.vcf`), which would need a concatenation step.

The user judged the RLE back-projection "way easier". For ancestry it is equivalent: PHG imputes one haplotype
per range, so every informative SNP in a range carries that range's ancestry. `hvcf2vcf` would add only the
literal VCF encoding and explicit calls at the no-call markers. It remains the route for when a real per-SNP
genotype file is needed. The stray per-range VCFs sit in `results/hvcf2vcf_introg/` on hazel.

## 7.5 Canonical tools found in zealhmm

The user pointed to existing functions that replace the ad-hoc code:

- zealhmm `R/metrics.R`: `rasterize_states(seg, grid)` projects segments onto a marker grid, and
  `marker_dsc(called, truth, grid, truth_raster)` gives per-class precision / recall / DSC, a `donor(>0)` row
  and `macro_dsc`.
- zealtiger `R/01_compile_map.R` `thin_markers` builds a 0.1 cM grid (about 1,190 markers on chr10 via the
  TeoNAM v5 map).
- zealhmm `scripts/zeal_export_release.R` writes a 0/1/2 matrix to TSV, VCF and PLINK.

The user decided that **for now only the painting is needed**. Visualization uses the RLE'd PHG. Rasterization
with `rasterize_states` and the 0.1 cM grid, the 012 matrices and the VCFs are parked for genetic mapping.
Marker-level DSC / MCC across callers has not been run.

| defect | evidence | cause as stated | status |
|---|---|---|---|

# 10. What was superseded

- **Per-taxon founders**, and the 3-founder graph with the taxon standing in → two-founder B73 + H_d (09-18).
- **Gene-only ranges** (memory note of 09-18) → lowcopy / union ranges, 8,095 on chr10 (09-20, kept on 09-21).
- **F = 0.86** with stay 0.9999 / 0.99 / 0.9991 → **F = 0, stay 0.99999** (09-22). This held after the grid,
  whose argmax (0.99 / 0.2) differs only marginally.
- **Excluding the B73 control from the score** → included (09-22, user).
- **PHG lane with gaps** → RLE-bridged, then gap-free fill (09-22).
